# test262 regular expression corpus

`test262.json` contains every distinct pattern and flag combination found in a
regular expression literal or a `RegExp` constructor under
`test/built-ins/RegExp` and `test/language/literals/regexp` at test262 commit
`7ab7fafa0003f73fc85c1b95d88094d33f7eb8bd`.

It was generated without committing the test262 checkout:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/tc39/test262.git /tmp/test262-regexp
git -C /tmp/test262-regexp checkout 7ab7fafa0003f73fc85c1b95d88094d33f7eb8bd
python3 internal/regexp/testdata/extract.py /tmp/test262-regexp internal/regexp/testdata/test262.json
```

The extractor scans literals and static constructor arguments, then executes
tests containing constructor calls in isolated realms to observe dynamically
assembled patterns. Each row is `[pattern, flags, source]`; equivalent pattern
and flag pairs are deduplicated. The Go oracle adds a deterministic generated
edge-case sweep and asks Node 24 whether constructing each expression throws a
`SyntaxError`.


The matcher execution corpus is `matches.json.gz`, generated by
`extract-matches.js` from the same pin using Node 24. Its captures are UTF-16
spans, with null for undefined captures; it also records named spans and
lastIndex. `matches-extraction.json` lists extraction failures, timeouts and
oversized input omissions. See `../MATCHER.md` for totals and reproduction.
The test262 BSD license is reproduced in `test262-license.txt`.
